entities.summary:
Pelagio Galvani was a Leonese cardinal and canon lawyer who played a pivotal role in shaping the medieval Catholic Church. He became a papal legate and leader of the Fifth Crusade, which aimed to retake Jerusalem from Muslim rule. This endeavor had significant implications for the Christian world, leading to increased tensions between Catholics and Muslims. As a result, Galvani's actions contributed to the escalation of the Crusades, which would have far-reaching consequences for European society.

Galvani's legacy extends beyond his involvement in the Fifth Crusade. He was a key figure in the development of canon law, which would go on to shape the Catholic Church's teachings and practices for centuries to come. As a cardinal, he held significant influence within the Church, using his position to promote the interests of the Church and the Catholic faithful.

In the end, Galvani's time came to an end, and he passed away on February 6, 1230. His death marked the end of an era, but his legacy lived on, influencing the course of Christian history for generations to come.
